name: Expressionist Architecture
summary: Buildings shaped as one plastic gesture of feeling. After the First World War, Mendelsohn, Taut, Poelzig and Höger used brick, concrete and glass to make crystals, caves and flowing masses.

philosophy.core_thesis: A building should carry an inner feeling in its form: the architect sculpts one dynamic mass, and the plan and the facade follow that gesture.
design_principles: Model the building as one continuous sculptural mass, with curved corners of radius 2 to 8m and no flat repeating wall.
Slope and fold the walls in diagonals of 60 to 80 degrees, so that the form seems to move.
Use brick, concrete or glass as a plastic material: cast, stacked or faceted, with no applied style.
Cut the openings as slots, triangles or bands that follow the form, not a grid.
Make an expressive crown or prow, 3 to 8m, that gives the building a single recognisable silhouette.
Treat daylight as a material: tint, split and concentrate it with glass, ribs and deep reveals.
anti_patterns: A flat repeating grid of identical windows
A plain rectangular box with a flat roof
Decoration pasted on a neutral wall
Right-angled corners with sharp edges everywhere

massing.form: One sculpted mass of curved, folded and stepped volumes, with a crown or prow as the focus.
massing.proportion: Heavy and low or crystalline and tall, never a regular box; the plan is 1.5 to 3 times the height.
massing.roof: A moulded or stepped crown, a dome, a spire or a rolled parapet, without a plain flat roof.
massing.relation_to_ground: Rooted in a broad base of 1 to 2m, with the walls swelling out of the ground.

structure.system: Brick, reinforced concrete or steel frame with a plastic skin, shaped by formwork and bricklayers.
structure.span_and_module: A span of 6 to 15m; a brick course of 0.07m; a column or rib every 3 to 4m.
structure.expression: The structure disappears into the form: the surface is the sculpture and the frame is hidden.

materials.finish: Plastic and heavy: dark brick, rendered concrete and tinted glass, shaped by hand and mould.

facade.composition: A single sweeping surface: the facade bends, folds or steps, and brick or render runs without a break.
facade.openings: Slots, triangles and bands that follow the curve; the window-to-wall ratio is 15 to 35%.

light_and_space.daylight: Light falls through tinted glass, ribbed domes and slit windows, and makes a dim, coloured, theatrical space.
light_and_space.spatial_sequence: A compressed entry opens into a high sculpted hall or stair, with curving ceilings and ribs.
light_and_space.interior_character: A ceiling of 4 to 12m, curved walls and vault-like surfaces, stalactite plaster and coloured light.

ornament.attitude: The form is the ornament: the mass, the brick pattern and the curved line carry all the expression.

rules.rule: Give the building one crown or prow that the eye reaches first.
Bend the brick courses and the ribs along the curve of the mass.
Make the mass heavy and monumental against the street.
Hold one material and one gesture over the whole form.
Place tinted glass and slots to light the main hall from above.
Set the dark solid mass against bright glass and render.

emotion.target_response: Awe and unease: the viewer feels a charged, dramatic form that seems alive.

use_cases: film set and game environment design
avoid_when: The brief needs a modular grid or a flexible plan.
The brief asks for calm, neutral architecture.

modifiers.how: Straighten the curves into planes, open the walls to a rational grid and drop the dark brick for white render.
Replace the plastic mass with stepped, symmetric forms and gilded geometric relief.

sources.title: Wolfgang Pehnt, Expressionist Architecture (Thames and Hudson, 1973)
